title: Who will lead Congress? Democrats weigh Schumer alternatives, Jeffries bid
gist: After Democrats flipped both chambers in the US midterms (54-44 Senate with two races uncalled; 253-161 House with 21 outstanding), a bloc of newly elected Democratic senators is refusing to back Chuck Schumer as majority leader, with some challengers being strong critics of the Iran war and US support for Israel (text truncated before the Jeffries section).

insights.claim: As of Friday after the midterms, Democrats had secured 54 Senate seats including two independents versus 44 for Republicans, with two races uncalled.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: A large Senate majority gives Democrats control over confirmations, treaties and war-powers votes.
insights.quote: Democrats have secured 54 Senate seats, including two independents, compared with 44 for Republicans

insights.claim: In the House, Democrats won 253 seats to Republicans' 161 with 21 races still outstanding — a lopsided majority.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Supermajority-scale House control raises odds of investigations and funding constraints on the administration's Iran policy.
insights.quote: In the House, Democrats have won 253 seats to Republicans’ 161, with 21 races still outstanding.

themes.theme: Revolt against Schumer and leadership shift

insights.claim: Newly elected Democratic senators from Maine, Kansas, Michigan and Illinois said they would not back Chuck Schumer as majority leader, amid growing calls for new leadership.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: A leadership change could shift Senate Democrats' stance on Israel and the Middle East.
insights.locator: A number of newly elected Democratic

insights.claim: Maine senator-elect Troy Jackson told Schumer he is going to support somebody else, and Kansas senator-elect Adam Hamilton and Illinois senator-elect Juliana Stratton also said they would not support him.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Count of defections is the key metric for whether Schumer survives.
insights.locator: A number of newly elected Democratic

insights.claim: Incoming Minnesota Sen. Peggy Flanagan and New Hampshire senator-elect Chris Pappas have called for new Democratic leadership.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Broadening opposition across progressive and swing-state members.
insights.locator: A number of newly elected Democratic

insights.claim: Moderates also want change: Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan said 'the old models do not work for people' and wants new party leadership; Schumer has led Senate Democrats since 2017.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Pressure for change spans ideological wings, raising odds of a leadership transition.
insights.quote: "the old models do not work for people"
insights.locator: Moderates have voiced calls for change

insights.claim: Several contenders challenging Schumer are strong critics of the Iran war and of US support to Israel.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: A new Senate leader could push harder to curb the Iran war and condition aid to Israel.
insights.quote: including strong critics of the Iran war and US support to Israel
insights.locator: A number of contenders have emerged
